newsitem.title: NORWAY: Aker RGI appeals against stock ruling.
newsitem.headline: Aker RGI appeals against stock ruling.

text.p: Norwegian industrial holding group Aker RGI ASA said on Tuesday it would appeal to the finance ministry against a ruling that the shareholdings of four investors in insurer Storebrand ASA would be seen as one entity.
A statement said the board of Aker RGI would appeal against last Friday's ruling of the Norwegian Banking, Insurance and Securities Commission.
"Aker RGI disagrees with the commission's view," it said.

The commission said the separate Storebrand shareholdings of billionaire Kjell Inge Roekke, his two companies Ivory Enterprises Corp and Ivory AS, as well as those of Aker RGI, of which Roekke is the main shareholder, amounted to one stake under Norwegian regulations.
The commission instructed Storebrand not to accept that this group held more than 10 percent of Storebrand shares.
Under Norwegian law any single shareholder or entity is not permitted to hold more than 10 percent in a financial institution.
The four entities together hold more than 16 percent in Storebrand.

The ruling backed a decision by Storebrand's board in April to combine the four shareholdings. The measure effectively curbed the voting rights of Roekke and his associates at Storebrand's annual general meeting.
Storebrand has been at odds with Roekke and Aker RGI since April when Aker RGI raised doubts about redeeming Storebrand's preference shares.
Aker RGI top executive Bjoern Rune Gjelsten, a close associate of Roekke, had questioned whether the rules for redeeming preference capital in Storebrand complied with securities legislation.
If Aker RGI's opinion prevailed, it could create problems in the proposed merger between Storebrand and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse ASA.
